question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s firm grip on the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced by the 2018 removal of presidential term limits and repeated purges of potential rivals, underpins the 95.5% trader consensus against his removal before 2027. At 73, he continues to lead publicly, including recent summits and state visits, while installing loyalists such as Cai Qi in key roles and deferring any successor discussion to the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027. Analysts across sources note the absence of credible internal challenges or institutional mechanisms for early transition, with the “seven up, eight down” retirement norm expected to apply mainly to others. While unverified health claims have circulated, no confirmed developments have altered his position. Rare scenarios that could still shift odds include a sudden incapacitating health event or an unprecedented elite power struggle before year-end.
